items.originalTitle: Code scanning AI Scan metrics in security overview

en.title: Code scanning AI Scan metrics in security overview
en.summary: Organization and enterprise administrators can now observe the impact of AI Scan for pull requests in security overview.
en.details:
Organization and enterprise administrators can now observe the impact of AI Scan for pull requests in security overview. New metrics show how many AI Scan findings were generated, resolved, the remediation rate, which repositories generated findings, trends over the selected reporting period, and how often developers applied autofix suggestions.

The “CodeQL pull requests” page is now named “Code scanning on pull requests” and includes separate CodeQL and AI Scan tabs. The AI Scan tab shows total findings and how many findings include or do not include an autofix suggestion. Metrics from the “CodeQL pull requests” page are now under the CodeQL tab.

These metrics help security teams evaluate the effectiveness of AI Scan across their organization or enterprise, understand developer response, and make informed rollout and investment decisions without reviewing individual pull requests.

This public preview is available on github.com, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud, for customers with GitHub Code Security or GitHub Advanced Security. GitHub Enterprise Server isn’t supported for this release.

Learn more about AI Scan for pull requests and join the AI Scan Community discussion .

The post Code scanning AI Scan metrics in security overview appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

en.title: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
en.summary: NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip.
en.details:
NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip. With up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, RTX Spark delivers the full stack of NVIDIA RTX and CUDA technologies for creators, developers and gamers, while unlocking a new paradigm in personal computing via powerful local AI agents.

Last week, NVIDIA and Microsoft announced that RTX Spark laptops will be available on Friday, Oct. 16 . Ahead of the launch, NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners are rolling out new software features and performance optimizations to expand what’s possible with local AI on RTX Spark.

New and upcoming RTX Spark updates — among the thousands of apps, games and models available at launch — include:

- New agent features, models and tools that enhance local agents on RTX Spark:

- Updates to top agent apps including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy streamline setup on RTX Spark, improve security with OpenShell and Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and enable hybrid local and cloud AI routing.

- The NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark, releases on Thursday, Oct. 15.

- NVIDIA PAIR moves out of beta and adds llama.cpp support.

en.title: From Earth to Orbit, France’s Ecosystem Delivers Agentic Computing at Scale With NVIDIA
en.summary: Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application.
en.details:
Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application.

France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork.

The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack.

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

Sovereign AI Infrastructure

France-based companies are expanding agentic infrastructure on NVIDIA technology.

Bull is extending its European AI server production to NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems, planned for 2028, with trays produced in Europe and rack integration at its Angers factory — inaugurated Friday, Oct. 2.

Altair-1, the first satellite in a $1 billion, 50-satellite constellation with on-board autonomous capabilities, launched this month and has successfully reached orbit. Integrated by Loft Orbital and built in Abu Dhabi by Orbitworks , a joint venture between Loft Orbital and Marlan Space , the satellite is flying NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge modules, running Mistral’s models, for real-time Earth observation and autonomous operations in orbit.
